thread:
marie_ae: Merchant POC — customer reporting slow TTFT on /chat after 10:15AM PDT. They're on dedicated pool (merchant-dedicated), model redwood-small-13b (q4_0). Also seeing occasional 429s. cc @tony_se @kevin_sre

tonv_se: On it — can you drop a minimal request + the runtime logs?

customer_engineer: Minimal repro: prompt ~60 tokens, expected response ~400 tokens. First token arrives ~2.1s, but end-to-end is 8–12s. No network timeouts on our side. We see sporadic 429: "rate_limit:queue_full" in our app logs.

anita_cs: Customer also asked about pricing for sustained 200 req/s over peak minute bursts. What ballpark commitment should I share?

kevin_sre: Quick glance at runtime: lots of KV cache misses + prefetch disabled. Logs show repeated lines like:
```
[2026-03-18T17:12:03Z] runtime: request=abc123 model=redwood-small-13b seq_len=512 kvcache::miss prefetch=false prefetch_queue=0
[2026-03-18T17:12:03Z] runtime: kernel=generic dispatch=blocked_by_batching slot_wait_ms=120 queue_size=14
[2026-03-18T17:12:04Z] limiter: rate_limit=200/s burst=50 queued=22 -> rate_limit:queue_full
```
Looks like prefetch turned off (customer/config). That explains the first-token okay but slow subsequent tokens due to KV misses and repeated kernel warmups.

marie_ae: They intentionally set prefetch=false for data residency concerns — they don't want persistent KV state. Can we offer a warmup approach that doesn't persist keys?

tony_se: Yes — two options: ephemeral prefetch (in-memory, not persisted) or controlled prefix warmup via preflight/prefetch API that evicts after session. Suggest: ephemeral prefetch + temporary warming script. Also bump batch_size to 4 and concurrency to 8 for their dedicated pool to reduce per-token overhead. Example warmup curl:
```bash
# run a lightweight prefix warmup (ephemeral)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/prefetch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-13b","prefixes":["<common_ua>"],"mode":"ephemeral","ttl_ms":300000}'
```
This warms the KV entries for typical prefixes without storing them long-term.

kevin_sre: Also check tokenization and system prompt size. Their app prepends a long user history which spikes seq_len and forces different kernel paths. We should enable dynamic_chunking/wavefront to keep kernel selection optimal. Short term: cap context to 1024 tokens for inference path.

ops_bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart on pool merchant-dedicated initiated by @kevin_sre (reason: apply ephemeral prefetch config).

billing_bot: Pricing note: sustained 200 req/s with dedicated baseline approximates ~$X/month depending on commit term and burst allowance. I'll run an exact quote and paste here.

customer_engineer: Data residency Q: ephemeral prefetch still touches model host memory. Is that acceptable for our legal team? We cannot write to external KV.

tony_se: Ephemeral prefetch keeps everything in local GPU process memory and never writes to external persistent stores. We can provide an audit snippet showing no writes to KVS. Also we can use per-request on-the-fly prefetching with TTL=0 so no durable state. Config example:
```json
{"kv": {"prefetch": {"mode": "ephemeral", "ttl_ms": 0, "max_entries": 2000}}}
```

anita_cs: I'll add a security note in the deal doc and send the vendor security questionnaire answer explaining ephemeral mode and no external persistence. Also capturing this for the onboarding checklist. :memo: 

marie_ae: OK — action items: (1) @tony_se provide warmup script + config, (2) @kevin_sre confirm kernel/dynamic_chunking tweak safe for q4_0 quantized model, (3) @billing_bot post formal quote for 200 req/s sustained with burst tolerance, (4) @anita_cs attach security note to the SOW. I'll follow up with customer tomorrow after warmup. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kevin_sre: Quick perf checklist I ran locally (for reference):
- enable ephemeral prefetch -> TTFT improved from ~2.1s to ~1.6s, tail down ~30%
- increase batch_size=4 -> throughput up, per-token overhead down
- cap seq_len=1024 for inference -> consistent kernel choice
- monitor prefetch_queue and limiter.

customer_engineer: Will try the warmup tonight and report results. Appreciate the quick turnaround team.

marie_ae: Great. I'll keep this thread updated. If warmup doesn't resolve, we can propose dedicated burst node or a short-term reserve to absorb spikes. :eyes:
